_comment: Authoring spec for gen-two-stage-corpus.mjs. T0 = concern-discovery state (no investigation results). T1 = decision-ready state (confirmed concern + findings the human actually established), NEVER the solution/outcome. Content is drawn from each GOAL's own 背景/调查结论 section, minus anything that is the chosen artifact.

cases.t0_rationale: Before the human had identified which code owns the lifecycle writes. Only the repo-shape signal is visible.
cases.t1_rationale: After the human had located the two write sites and established the placement constraint, but before any artifact existed. 5 min before activatedAt.
cases.timeline_note: GOAL-030 is the first real goal-branch pilot; the human's driving goal was MECHANISM validation, not architectural payoff. That intent is T0-visible (it is in the trigger).

t0_context.repo_state_summary: The goal-branch mechanism exists but has never carried a real development direction through its full lifecycle (GOAL-901..905 were rehearsals; GOAL-905's merge needed 6 suite retries). Separately, task lifecycle status is written directly inside orchestration-layer scripts; there is no single decision layer and no structured per-transition record.
code_pointers: plugin/scripts/ready-pool-check.ts (contains the status-write logic for both promote and retreat directions; function names not resolved here)
t0_context.prior_goal_precedents_note: First real (non-rehearsal) goal-branch pilot; no prior real sample exists.
known_mechanism_risks: Two earlier incidents show worktree-loaded code silently resolving to the main checkout (Core plugin-root relocation; quay-native via a node_modules symlink) — a worktree is not guaranteed to run its own code.
SPEC-goal-branch 4.10/8: preview instances do not run the driver, and a goal changing driver code gets no pre-merge trial.
t0_context.test_suite_state: scripts/test.sh green on develop at the cutoff commit.

cases.concern: Task lifecycle status writes (todo->ready and ready->todo) live inside orchestration-layer scripts with no single decision layer and no structured per-transition record; and the goal-branch mechanism itself has never been proven on a real development direction.
t1_findings: The two write sites are applyPromotions (todo->ready, promote edge) and applyRevaluations (ready->todo, retreat edge), both inside plugin/scripts/ready-pool-check.ts.
The lifecycle edge table currently lives in gate/lifecycle.ts; the status-field patch helper lives in plugin/scripts/task-ops.ts and already has 4 call sites.
fan-in has 4 separate status-write sites, and the needs-human/branch-sync-alignment path has 2 more. Both are deliberately out of scope for this first trial.
The mechanism risk is load-bearing: proving a worktree/preview actually runs its own branch's code is an explicit acceptance condition, not an assumption.
not_at_T1: The chosen new module path and symbol names.
Whether the sink layer should be the kernel, and the resulting edge-count delta.

t1_context.goal_branch_mechanism_state: Rehearsals only; the human has decided to use this refactor as the first REAL pilot of the mechanism, with health gating any scope growth.
t1_context.existing_shared_data: the lifecycle edge table in gate/lifecycle.ts; the status-field patch helper in plugin/scripts/task-ops.ts (4 call sites)
t1_context.deliberately_excluded: fan-in (4 write sites) and needs-human/branch-sync alignment (2 write sites)
t1_context.placement_constraint_established_during_: Both packages/* and plugin/scripts must be able to reach the shared decision point without introducing a reverse dependency edge.
t1_context.test_suite_state: scripts/test.sh green on develop at the cutoff commit.

expected_concerns: lifecycle status writes scattered across orchestration scripts with no single decision layer / no structured per-transition record
the goal-branch mechanism is unproven on a real development direction (mechanism-level concern)
plugin/scripts reaches the kernel on far fewer edges than it does non-kernel modules (boundary under-use)

stage_b_ref.rationale: At T1 both write sites are located and the placement constraint is established, so the remaining work is execution, not discovery. Saying 'investigate' at T1 would be under-committing.
stage_b_ref.min_sufficiency: Both directions of the promotion path share one decision point and one event schema; splitting promote/retreat into two goals would double branch-lifecycle overhead for no independent acceptance benefit. Broadening to fan-in's 4 sites would add debugging surface on the first real trial of the mechanism itself — the thing actually being tested.
alternatives: Sink only the promote edge (todo->ready) first, leaving retreat for a follow-up — defensible if the goal is to minimise blast radius further, but it halves the evidence that the event schema generalises.

Model the transition decision as a pure data table owned by the kernel and write events from each call site without a shared writer function — defensible, weaker on the 'single decision layer' half of the concern.
adjacent: Cover the needs-human/branch-sync alignment writes in the same pass (rejected: different mechanism, doubles surface)
too_broad: Refactor all six lifecycle write sites (promotion x2, fan-in x4, needs-human x2) at once
Full OO/domain ownership analysis of the orchestration layer
too_fragmented: Create one goal per single status literal
Add an event writer without unifying the decision point
stage_b_ref.predicted_delta: plugin/scripts -> kernel edge strength rises by the number of switched call sites; each transition emits one structured event
stage_b_ref.observed_delta: Not recorded in the case fixture; AC-339's before/after used a single-root archguard analysis with an on/off kernel-import control.

cases.t0_rationale: Before the human classified any of the raw dispersion hits. The raw tool output is visible; its interpretation is not.
cases.t1_rationale: After the human had classified each hit as genuine / exempted / false-positive and corrected the numeric target from <=2 to 4.
cases.timeline_note: The human's own origin line records that the original technical premise was wrong and was corrected BEFORE activation. That correction is the T1 content.

t0_context.repo_state_summary: GOAL-030 has landed. The project's ownership-first method calls for small independently-verifiable slices.

archguard_literal_dispersion.note: Raw output only. Whether each hit is a genuine un-migrated consumer, a legitimate exemption, or a false positive has NOT been determined.

code_pointers: plugin/scripts/goal-driver.ts — grep -c 'status === "needs-human"' returns 6 at this cutoff; not yet classified
t0_context.test_suite_state: scripts/test.sh green on develop at the cutoff commit.

cases.concern: A bare 'needs-human' status literal is dispersed across several modules; whether that indicates genuinely un-migrated consumers or merely look-alike strings has not been determined.
t1_findings: task-status.ts is the canonical declaration itself — its occurrence is not a defect.
github-client.ts is already explicitly exempted by a prior task: an independent provider package cannot statically import abi.ts, and its literal shape is pinned by its own needle test.
observation.ts and workflow-baseline-metrics.ts are FALSE POSITIVES: they compare a different vocabulary (a promotion-outcome 'action' field and a workflow 'outcome' field), not task.status.

goal-driver.ts holds the only genuine un-migrated residue: 5 of its 6 occurrences are real task.status comparisons; the 6th compares a GOAL-AC status field (a different vocabulary) and must stay untouched.
Therefore the achievable dispersion floor is 4, not 2 — the canonical declaration and the two false-positive files are permanent residues, and the exemption is fixed.
The original numeric target (<=2) was unachievable and has been corrected.
not_at_T1: Any statement of which module the 5 literals should consume, or the resulting grep count.

t1_context.classified_dispersion: 5 raw hits = 1 canonical declaration + 1 explicit provider exemption + 2 false positives (different vocabulary) + 1 file with genuine residue
t1_context.genuine_residue: plugin/scripts/goal-driver.ts: 6 occurrences of the literal, of which 5 are genuine task.status comparisons and 1 is a GOAL-AC status (different vocabulary, out of scope)
t1_context.existing_canonical_source: packages/quay/src/abi.ts (packages tree) + plugin/scripts/task-status.ts (plugin tree); 16 consumers already migrated by a prior DONE task
t1_context.corrected_target: achievable dispersion floor is 4, not the originally assumed 2
t1_context.user_constraint_recorded: do not sweep unrelated status literals (todo/ready/done) in the same file, even for style consistency
t1_context.test_suite_state: scripts/test.sh green on develop at the cutoff commit.

expected_concerns: dispersed literal for one status value across modules, canonical home unclear
possible duplicated/parallel vocabulary declarations between the packages tree and the plugin tree

stage_b_ref.rationale: At T1 every hit is classified and the achievable target is corrected, so the slice is fully specified; the remaining work is a mechanical substitution.
stage_b_ref.min_sufficiency: All 5 genuine occurrences are the identical mechanical substitution in one file, and the correct canonical source already exists and is already used by 16 consumers. Splitting per-occurrence multiplies branch-lifecycle overhead for a change no reviewer can accept piecemeal; broadening to the false-positive files or to unrelated literals would touch things that are not defects.
alternatives: Route all status comparisons in goal-driver.ts through the canonical module in one pass (rejected by the recorded user constraint: todo/ready/done literals must stay).
Introduce a shared Verdict/Status primitive instead of consuming the existing module (rejected: that is a second declaration, not convergence).
adjacent: Converge mcp-server.ts's hand-copied kind enumeration (a different vocabulary, out of scope)
too_broad: Convert every status literal in the repo
Touch the false-positive files or the exempted provider
stage_b_ref.predicted_delta: dispersion count drops by the number of genuine un-migrated consumers; the grep count for the literal in goal-driver.ts falls correspondingly
stage_b_ref.observed_delta: dispersion 5 -> 4 and the goal-driver.ts count 6 -> 1, with each of the 4 residual hits individually justified as a non-defect.

cases.t0_rationale: The duplicate-detection hit is visible; the equivalence question is entirely open.
cases.t1_rationale: After the equivalence investigation concluded (the human's own origin line states the goal was created AFTER the conclusion). 5 min before activatedAt.
cases.timeline_note: This case is the clearest T0/T1 example in the corpus: the v1 input already carried an investigation conclusion under a T0 cutoff, which is exactly the hindsight mismatch the redesign removes.

t0_context.repo_state_summary: GOAL-030 and GOAL-031 have landed. ArchGuard detect_duplicates flags one duplicate-implementation group.

archguard_duplicate_group.surface_similarity: Both parsers follow the same shape: non-zero exit => not-evaluated; bare token match; scan upward from the last line for a JSON verdict object; otherwise not-evaluated.
archguard_duplicate_group.note: Structural similarity does NOT establish semantic equivalence. The classification has not been made at this cutoff.

prior_goal_precedents.one_line: status-literal convergence with a corrected target; landed.

t0_context.test_suite_state: scripts/test.sh green on develop at the cutoff commit.

cases.concern: A duplicate-implementation group flagged by detect_duplicates spans a packages/ parser and a plugin/ parser; whether they are semantically equivalent or intentionally divergent is undetermined.
t1_findings: The two parsers are STRUCTURALLY IDENTICAL and semantically EQUIVALENT (not intentionally-divergent): the algorithm is byte-for-byte the same shape, and the only difference is which two literal strings count as the positive/negative verdict values.

This is deliberate copying, not convergent evolution: criterion-fidelity.ts's own source comment says it reuses goal-driver.ts's fail-closed approach verbatim, and a test file independently describes the parser as mirroring it.

The PARSER ALGORITHM is domain-agnostic — 'parse a judge's raw stdout into a three-state verdict, fail closed if unreadable' does not depend on whether the domain is fidelity or sufficiency; the legal-value word list is DATA, not logic.

The two CALLERS' orchestration genuinely differs and should stay different (one synchronous/uncached via an injected judge seam; one async, two-sample-agreement before caching, with split failure causes).
Kernel placement is reachable from both trees without creating a reverse edge (the principle established by GOAL-030).
not_at_T1: The chosen new module path and the generic function's name/signature.

t1_context.equivalence_verdict: equivalent (identical algorithm; only the two legal-value literals differ)
t1_context.evidence_of_deliberate_copy: criterion-fidelity.ts source comment claims verbatim reuse; a sibling test file independently describes mirroring it
t1_context.domain_agnosticism: the parse algorithm is independent of which verdict vocabulary is passed in
t1_context.placement_principle: kernel is reachable from both packages/ and plugin/ without a reverse edge
t1_context.test_suite_state: scripts/test.sh green on develop at the cutoff commit.

expected_concerns: a duplicate implementation of one concept exists across the packages/plugin boundary and has no single owner
the equivalence question is unresolved, so any merge is premature

stage_b_ref.rationale: The equivalence investigation is COMPLETE as of T1, so 'investigate' would re-do finished work. Note the trap the v1 benchmark fell into: it labelled this 'goal' while feeding a T0 state, which made 'investigate' look wrong for the right reason.
stage_b_ref.min_sufficiency: Converging only one of the two call sites does not clear the duplicate-detection finding at all — the minimal unit that resolves the signal is both sides sharing one implementation. Nothing smaller is still a complete answer; nothing larger is needed because the callers' orchestration legitimately differs and the other verdict types are a separate, larger gap.
alternatives: Sink the shared algorithm and keep both callers unchanged (the selected approach) — zero caller churn.
Sink the algorithm AND unify the two callers' orchestration — rejected: over-generalises, the orchestration difference is intentional.
Leave the duplication and record it as an accepted cross-tree exemption — defensible only if the two were intentionally divergent, which T1 rules out.
adjacent: The ~27 dispersed literal files for other verdict types (a separate, larger gap)
too_broad: Unify all verdict-shaped types in one pass
Merge the two callers' orchestration as well as the parser
Touch the packages/ directory-cycle issue in the same goal
too_fragmented: Convert only one of the two call sites
Add a shared helper without making either original function delegate to it
stage_b_ref.predicted_delta: the duplicate-detection group disappears and the canonical definition count for this algorithm drops to one, with both call chains confirmed to have actually changed what they call
stage_b_ref.observed_delta: Duplicate group cleared; canonical-definition count for the shared algorithm 2 -> 1; both call chains independently verified to delegate.

cases.t0_rationale: The single package-level SCC is visible from the cycle reading; which edge is cheapest to cut, and what else leaves with it, is not established.
cases.t1_rationale: After the human had enumerated the exact edges in both directions and the zero-inbound property of every other SCC member. 5 min before activatedAt.
cases.timeline_note: CRITICAL hindsight control: the real T1 belief was that the SCC would go 6 -> 5 with the other five members unchanged. The later measurement showed 6 -> 4 because fan-in's only in-edge was through cli. That correction is recorded as OUTCOME only and must not appear in the T1 input.

t0_context.repo_state_summary: GOAL-030/031/032 have landed. ArchGuard detect_cycles(outputScope: package) reports exactly one package-level cycle.

archguard_cycle_reading.reading_at_cutoff: exactly one package-level cycle exists: a 6-member SCC comprising the packages/quay/src root, cli, fan-in, gate, gate/config, gate/factories.
archguard_cycle_reading.note: Which single edge is the cheapest to cut, and what else would leave the SCC with it, has NOT been established.

t0_context.draft_layers_rule: An unlanded draft layers.yml already lists the root<->cli edge as a known violation and recommends tightening it, but does not decide how.
t0_context.test_suite_state: scripts/test.sh green on develop at the cutoff commit.

cases.concern: One package-level dependency cycle (a 6-member SCC) exists, and the root<->cli edge is the outermost, cheapest candidate to cut; the ownership question is which side should own the shared primitives the edge crosses.
t1_findings: core-root -> cli is exactly 2 value edges, both static paths, confirmed by grep and by the package fan-in reading (fanIn = 2): one imports a driver control client into a session handler; the other imports a service-name vocabulary into the server entry — of which one imported symbol is entirely unused (a dead import).
cli -> core-root is the normal direction with 34 edges and is not itself a problem.
Every other SCC member (gate, gate/config, gate/factories, fan-in, primitives, kernel) contributes ZERO edges into cli.
Therefore removing those 2 edges leaves cli with no inbound edge from inside the cycle, so cli MUST leave the SCC.

The ownership reading: this is not CLI reaching backward into core, nor core wanting a CLI facade — two primitives genuinely shared by both layers were placed under cli/ only because their first historical consumer was CLI help text.
not_at_T1: The chosen destination module paths and symbol names for the two moved primitives.
The fan-in collateral effect discovered later (that fan-in's only in-edge was through cli, so it leaves the SCC too) — at T1 the belief was that the other five members were unchanged.
The measured before/after SCC membership and the negative-control result.

t1_context.root_to_cli_edges: exactly 2, both static value edges (one control-client import used by a session handler; one service-name vocabulary import at the server entry, one symbol of which is dead)
t1_context.other_members_to_cli_edges: 0 (gate, gate/config, gate/factories, fan-in, primitives, kernel all contribute none)
t1_context.derived_property: after removing the 2 root->cli edges, cli has no inbound edge from within the cycle, so it must leave the SCC
t1_context.ownership_reading: two primitives shared by both layers were filed under cli/ because their first consumer was CLI help text
t1_context.test_suite_state: scripts/test.sh green on develop at the cutoff commit.

expected_concerns: a package-level dependency cycle indicates an ownership inversion somewhere among its members
two primitives shared by two layers have no unambiguous owner
a draft layers rule exists but is unlanded, so a declared boundary is documented but not enforced

stage_b_ref.rationale: At T1 the exact edges in both directions are enumerated and the zero-inbound property of the other members is established, so the cut is specified. 'Investigate' would repeat finished work.
stage_b_ref.min_sufficiency: The two root->cli edges must move together — they are consumed in combination by the same downstream call sites, and moving one alone leaves a partially-converged state with no independent acceptance story. Broadening to the other five SCC members would require re-deciding ownership for all of them at once, which is a far larger and riskier undertaking than cutting the one cheapest, best-understood edge.
alternatives: Cut the two edges and sink both shared primitives to the root layer (the selected approach).

Keep the primitives under cli/ and invert instead by making cli own the composition surface — defensible if cli is the true owner, but the T1 ownership reading says the two primitives are shared, not CLI-specific.
Land the draft layers rule first as a declared-rule gate and cut later — defensible as a smaller first step, but it enforces nothing until the edge is actually gone.
adjacent: The needs-human / branch-sync status-alignment writes (a different mechanism, already excluded by GOAL-030)
too_broad: Clear the entire 6-member SCC in one goal
Re-decide ownership for gate, gate/config, gate/factories and fan-in simultaneously
too_fragmented: Move only one of the two edges
Relocate a single symbol rather than the shared primitive as a unit
stage_b_ref.predicted_delta: the package SCC shrinks and cli's package fan-in from the root falls to zero; the other cycle members unchanged
stage_b_ref.observed_delta: SCC 6 -> 4 (not the predicted 5): cli AND fan-in both left, because fan-in's only in-edge inside the cycle was through cli/driver.ts. The other four members were unchanged, and a negative control (re-injecting one used root->cli edge) brought cli back in.
